title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page belongs to the genus-0 part of the Teichmüller-groupoid notes. M_{0,n} is the complement of a complexified real arrangement (the braid arrangement). Grothendieck is setting up an elementary 'real' description of paths in such complements. The page is sandwiched between university budget sheets (used as scrap paper).

Notation (reconstructed):
- V is a real affine plane (more generally a real affine space) and V_C its complexification.
- R : V_C → V is the real-part projection.
- For a real line Δ ⊂ V, Δ_C is its complexification, and R(Δ_C) = Δ, since Δ_C = Δ + i·dir(Δ).
- φ_ω (ω a vector of V) is presumably the map V → V_C, x ↦ x + iω, pushing a real point off the real locus in the imaginary direction ω.
- V^{**} presumably denotes V minus the union of the lines of the arrangement (real chambers).

Lemma 2 (trivial). Take x, y ∈ V and a path ℓ : x → y in V. Consider the homotopy g(s,t) (written something like (1−s)φ_ω ℓ…; most plausibly g(s,t) = ℓ(t) + i(1−s)ω). Its real part is always ℓ(t), so R(g([0,1]²)) = |ℓ|. If |ℓ| ∩ Δ = ∅, then g([0,1]²) ∩ Δ_C = ∅, because R(Δ_C) = Δ.

Corollary. If ℓ is a path in V^{**}, the following square commutes up to homotopy in V_C minus the union of the Δ_C:
- top: the path φ_ω(ℓ) from φ_ω(x) to φ_ω(y);
- bottom: ℓ from x to y;
- verticals: the straight 'imaginary' segments L_{x,φ_ω(x)} and L_{y,φ_ω(y)}.
So real paths avoiding the real lines can be transported to any imaginary shift.

Lemma 3 (±trivial). Define the standard path ℓ_{y,x} from x to y by
ℓ(t) = x + t(y−x) + i·sin(πt)(y−x)/2.
It is an arc whose real part is the segment [x,y] and whose imaginary part is parallel to y−x. Claim: |ℓ_{y,x}| ∩ Δ_C = ∅ for every real line Δ not meeting {x,y}.

Proof (as on the page):
1. Suppose some point ℓ(t) lies in Δ_C. Taking real parts, Δ ∩ [x,y] ≠ ∅. Since x, y ∉ Δ, we get Δ ∩ [x,y] = {a} with a ≠ x, y, and t ≠ 0, 1.
2. The imaginary part sin(πt)(y−x)/2 is nonzero and must lie in dir(Δ). So y−x is parallel to Δ.
3. With a ∈ Δ on the line xy, this forces line(x,y) = Δ, hence x, y ∈ Δ. Absurd.

The argument is correct. Each pair of real points therefore gets a canonical 'complex detour' path. In the actual application, x and y lie off all lines and the path must avoid every Δ_C of the arrangement. This is the standard device for building the fundamental groupoid of a complexified real arrangement complement with base points in the real chambers, as in Deligne 1972 and Salvetti 1987. It also fits Grothendieck's use of real/tangential base points for the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid.
errors: The formula for g is garbled on the page. As written, '(1−s)φ_ω ℓ(s) + ℓ(t)' mixes variables. The intended homotopy is surely ℓ(t) + i(1−s)ω (or equivalently (1−s)φ_ω(ℓ(t)) + sℓ(t)). With that reading the real-part argument is fine.
The page writes ℓ_{x,y}(t) = (sin t)(y−x)/2. This must mean the imaginary part, with sin(πt) for t ∈ [0,1]. Minor notational slip.
Lemma 3 as stated only treats single lines not meeting {x,y}. The proof is correct but sketchy: it does not explicitly note that sin(πt) ≠ 0 for t ∈ (0,1).

ideas.what: Using the real-part projection R: V_C → V to show that homotopies whose real part avoids the real lines avoid their complexifications
ideas.modern_name: Real structure / real-part projection argument for complexified real hyperplane arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1972, Immeubles des groupes de tresses généralisés); Salvetti (1987)

ideas.what: Canonical 'arc' paths ℓ_{y,x} between real points via an imaginary semicircle-like detour parallel to y−x, avoiding complexified lines not through x, y
ideas.modern_name: Standard paths between chambers in the complement of a complexified real arrangement (Salvetti complex / Deligne groupoid of chambers)

ideas.what: Real points (chambers) as base points for the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,n}-type spaces
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid with real/tangential base points (dihedral chambers of M_{0,n}(R))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme), Deligne (1989, tangential base points), Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of the Teichmüller tower and base points

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, self-described 'trivial' lemmas about paths in complexified real line-arrangement complements. These are standard, done by Deligne 1972 and later Salvetti. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The header reads 'Lemme 2 (trivial)' followed by a crossed-out word and then 'Posons' (?) 'pour x, y ∈ V'.
'ℓ_{x,y}(t) = (sin t)(y−x)/2' should be read as Im ℓ_{x,y}(t) = sin(πt)(y−x)/2.
In 'g_{[-x,y-]}', the struck subscript is likely 'x,y'. The formula intended is likely g(s,t) = ℓ(t) + i(1−s)ω, i.e. built from (1−s)φ_ω and ℓ(t).
The Corollary line likely reads 'Si ℓ est un chemin dans V^{**}, on a un diagramme commutatif (à homotopie près)'.

The proof of Lemma 3 likely reads: 'Car si on avait |ℓ_{y,x}| ∩ Δ_C ≠ ∅, on aurait (comme Δ ∩ {x,y} = ∅) Δ ∩ [x,y] ≠ ∅, donc ... ; Δ ∩ [x,y] = {a}, a ≠ x,y, a = R ℓ_{x,y}(t), t ≠ 0,1; alors Im ℓ_{x,y}(t) = sin(πt)(y−x)/2, donc y−x ∈ direction de Δ, donc x, y ∈ Δ (droite des translations de Δ), absurde'.
